Hydrology of Quiet Coves

HYDROLOGY_ARTICLE_SENTENCE records how a pocket beach traps freshwater seepage after storms. Tidal stage, rainfall, and a buried paleochannel together set the salinity of the back-barrier pond. Observers sampled the pond every six hours for two spring tides and logged conductivity, temperature, and dissolved organic carbon so the time series could be compared with the nearby gauging station.

Seepage faces appear at low tide as dark bands of saturated sand. Dye traces confirmed that dune groundwater, not the lagoon, feeds those bands. Grain-size maps show a fining-landward trend that matches the seepage hypothesis rather than a washover origin. Additional sentences keep this cluster well above the readability character threshold used by the Mozilla parser.

Field methods

Piezometers were driven to one metre. Each stilling well had a vented pressure transducer logging at one-minute intervals. Surveyed staff plates provided an independent check.
